gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured range for any candidate kit. The only named figures I found are KayakCambria's (author 'Cubby', updated 2026-05-13): 47 miles of mixed terrain to BMS cutoff for the Cloudenergy 48V 105Ah, 38–42 miles on hilly terrain for the DC House 48V 100Ah on a Yamaha G29, and about 8 more miles than lead-acid for the Vatrer 48V 105Ah on a modified Club Car Precedent.
standout_why: I opened golfcartgearlab.com (updated 2026-11-11), cartvoltage.com (updated 2026-10-27), golfcartshowdown.com and cartvolts.com/compare. All four say they do not test products ('we don't test products ourselves', 'we don't run a test lab', 'we don't bench-test them'). None reports a capacity, range, sag or charge-time measurement for any kit. gearranking.com would not load (certificate error), so I couldn't check it. In strict terms the KayakCambria figures are new, which would score a 2. I scored 1 because they are weak: the method isn't described, three of the results are on carts other than Club Cars, the Vatrer figure only compares against a neighbour's old lead-acid pack, and the page has internal inconsistencies (a 'November 2026' header on a page last updated in May 2026, and ratings that conflict between sections). That makes them hard to defend as a deciding fact.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. None of ChatGPT's three picks (Vatrer 105Ah Club Car kit, LiTime 100Ah kit, Redodo 100Ah kit) has a named independent capacity or range measurement I could open and read. The page can say honestly that every capacity and range figure for these kits is the maker's claim, and that the only named range figures (KayakCambria) cover Cloudenergy and DC House, not LiTime or Redodo. If kept at all, the Cloudenergy 47-mile figure is the one usable data point for the cheaper 105Ah alternative ChatGPT showed at $1,199.99.
